name: streak-calendar

frames.best_why: Shows all three views at once with the year heatmap, month grid and week row fully visible.

tagline: Year heatmap, month grid and week row mark days of a streak.
summary: A streak tracker drawn three ways: a 365-day contribution heatmap, a month grid and a current-week row. Active days fill in, used freezes turn blue, today is ringed and future days dim.
appearance: Three bordered dark cards. A wide year heatmap of tiny rounded squares runs in week columns, below it a seven-column month grid with weekday letters, and beside that a row of seven circles captioned with weekday names. Filled days are pale, freeze days bright blue.
behaviour: Each view paints the streak periods it is given: active days fill, freeze days tint blue, today gets a ring and future days fade out. Hovering a year cell opens a date tooltip, and every day is a button that can report a click and takes a focus ring.
demo_content: November 2026 and a 12-day streak, generated relative to the current date.
search_phrases: daily streak grid in three views
heatmap of days with freeze days
use_when: A habit or learning app needs a whole year of daily activity at a glance, with a close-up month and week.
avoid_when: It only draws the periods you pass: it calculates no streak, has no month navigation and no data fetching.
customise: Streak periods arrive as an array of date ranges; view, month, reference date, start of week, freeze visibility and a day-click handler are props. Cell sizing stays in the source.
weight_why: About 365 small cells plus a tooltip each; nothing animates after the first render.

a11y.note: Cells expose full date labels and grid roles, but nothing explains that the blue squares are freezes.

issues: The month card's bottom row is clipped by the crop, leaving the last days half cut.
The year heatmap has no legend, so the blue freeze squares carry no explanation.
polish_why: Coherent three-view system with clear active and freeze colours; no legend and a clipped month row.
title: Streak Calendar
